svg.text: World scale: the decision, and what shipped
Everything below is drawn at one shared scale. Side views are true 1:1 — no vertical exaggeration, so the slopes you see are the real slopes.
Both vents measured the same way: on bare seafloor.
68 m radius, 52 m cap: 97 m of island at a 43° flank
272 m radius: 390 m of island at a 13° flank
The target it was aiming at
“shields across” = how many 544 m plausible shields fit edge to edge.
Below 1.00 the grid cannot hold a single shield at all.
“jump resolve” is measured. C's figure is the shipped one: the ocean-current
pressure solve costs side³ and would have made C cost 3.62 s on its own, so
it was decoupled from the terrain grid. B's figure is pre-decoupling.
Cells get coarser as the world gets wider: a stream valley is a few cells across,
so C's 5 m cell buys width by giving up some drainage detail.
same scale in all three — a shield is genuinely this flat
AFTER, measured by running the shipping accretion code: a vigorous vent breaks the surface as an island 390 m wide and 46 m tall — a 13° mean flank, with single steps up to 58°.
A real Galápagos shield is about 10°. Built onto the starting island rather than onto bare seafloor — the gameplay case — the same vent gives 790 m of land at 6.6°.
